title: Exact-Fp/Z Cartier-Operator, Laurent Pole-Cancellation, and Residue-Pin Eigenvector Certificates with a Machine-Checked Integer Kernel
abstract: Motivated by characteristic-p Cartier-operator boundary extraction and residue-pin eigenvector constructions in border algebraic complexity, we present an explicitly scoped, standalone, zero-floating-point verification stack pairing two layers. Layer 1 (BorderVPVNPResidues.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 18 theorems, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 warnings) proves exact integral Frobenius additivity defects for p in {2,3,5}, Fermat's little theorem on Z/3Z and Z/5Z, elementary Cartier exponent-index arithmetic (p(-1)+(p-1)=-1, injectivity, shift, non-(p-1) exclusion), scalar pole cancellation (r_1+P)+(r_2-P)=r_1+r_2, 2x2 integer eigenvector linearity, explicit hinge-shortening gap amplification (gap := 2Dm - (w + 2D*l) >= 1), batched query list-sum budgets, the 2x2 entrywise determinant triangle bound |a00*a11 - a01*a10| <= 2B^2, and inductive 2^{u^5} > (2^{u^4})^k over u, k in N. Layer 2 (BORDER-VPVNP-CERT-1.0, pure-stdlib Python exact-Fp/Z auditor) provides a self-contained four-mode verifier checking exact prime-field Cartier semilinearity C_p(A^p eta) = A C_p(eta) and Res(C_p eta) = Res(eta) across p = 3..29, cancelling Laurent poles up to order 10, d x d (d in {3,4,6,8}) pin-eigenvector systems over F_p, and finite hinge/2x2-minor/exponent witnesses across 16 canonical certificates (0.024-0.305 ms) while rejecting 54/54 live adversarial forgeries.
